content: 1. Diagnostic tools should be selected based on their general characteristics, such as low, moderate, or high complexity, rather than focusing on specific products. This includes considering the infrastructure, equipment, and technical skills required, as well as the target conditions, such as tuberculosis (TB) and resistance to first-line or second-line drugs, or both. Factors like turnaround times, throughput, existing infrastructure, specimen referral networks, economic aspects, and qualitative aspects such as acceptability, equity, and end-user preferences should also be taken into account. 2. This document provides background information, justification, and recommendations for novel diagnostic tools aimed at detecting Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex (MTBC) and identifying mutations in target genes associated with anti-TB drug resistance. 3. The intended audience for these guidelines includes laboratory managers, clinicians, healthcare staff, HIV and TB program managers, policymakers, technical agencies, donors, and implementing partners supporting TB diagnostics in resource-limited settings. It is also useful for individuals involved in program planning, budgeting, resource mobilization, and training activities for managing drug-resistant TB. 4. The development of the Xpert MTB/RIF assay (Cepheid, Sunnyvale, USA) marked a significant advancement in improving TB diagnosis and detecting rifampicin resistance globally. However, its sensitivity is suboptimal, particularly in smear-negative and HIV-associated TB cases. To address these limitations, Cepheid developed the Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra assay (Xpert Ultra), which uses the same GeneXpert® platform as the original assay. 5. Recommendations are provided for five specific types of testing, categorized by initial or repeated testing and the type of TB (pulmonary or extrapulmonary). 6. In adults with signs and symptoms of pulmonary TB, Xpert MTB/RIF should be used as the initial diagnostic test for TB and rifampicin resistance detection in sputum, rather than smear microscopy, culture, and phenotypic drug susceptibility testing (DST). This is a strong recommendation with high certainty of evidence for test accuracy and moderate certainty for patient-important outcomes. 7. In children with signs and symptoms of pulmonary TB, Xpert MTB/RIF should be used as the initial diagnostic test for TB and rifampicin resistance detection in sputum, gastric aspirate, nasopharyngeal aspirate, and stool, rather than smear microscopy, culture, and phenotypic DST. This is a strong recommendation with moderate certainty of evidence for sputum accuracy and low certainty for other specimen types. 8. In adults with signs and symptoms of pulmonary TB and no prior history of TB (≤5 years) or a remote history of TB treatment (>5 years since treatment completion), Xpert Ultra should be used as the initial diagnostic test for TB and rifampicin resistance detection in sputum, rather than smear microscopy, culture, and phenotypic DST. This is a strong recommendation with high certainty of evidence for test accuracy. 9. In adults with signs and symptoms of pulmonary TB and a prior history of TB treatment within the last 5 years, Xpert Ultra may be used as the initial diagnostic test for TB and rifampicin resistance detection in sputum, rather than smear microscopy, culture, and phenotypic DST. This is a conditional recommendation with low certainty of evidence for test accuracy. 10. In children with signs and symptoms of pulmonary TB, Xpert Ultra should be used as the initial diagnostic test for TB and rifampicin resistance detection in sputum or nasopharyngeal aspirate, rather than smear microscopy, culture, and phenotypic DST. This is a strong recommendation with low certainty of evidence for sputum accuracy and very low certainty for nasopharyngeal aspirate accuracy. 11. For TB meningitis, Xpert MTB/RIF or Xpert Ultra should be used in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) as the initial diagnostic test, rather than smear microscopy or culture. This is a strong recommendation with moderate certainty of evidence for Xpert MTB/RIF accuracy and low certainty for Xpert Ultra accuracy. 12. For extrapulmonary TB, Xpert MTB/RIF may be used in lymph node aspirate, lymph node biopsy, pleural fluid, peritoneal fluid, pericardial fluid, synovial fluid, or urine specimens as the initial diagnostic test, rather than smear microscopy or culture. This is a conditional recommendation with varying levels of certainty depending on the specimen type. 13. In HIV-positive adults and children with signs and symptoms of disseminated TB, Xpert MTB/RIF may be used in blood as an initial diagnostic test. This is a conditional recommendation with very low certainty of evidence for test accuracy. 14. In adults with signs and symptoms of pulmonary TB who have an Xpert Ultra trace positive result on the initial test, repeated testing with Xpert Ultra may not be used. This is a conditional recommendation with very low certainty of evidence for test accuracy. 15. In children with signs and symptoms of pulmonary TB in settings with a pretest probability of 5% or more and an Xpert MTB/RIF negative result on the initial test, repeated testing with Xpert MTB/RIF (for a total of two tests) in sputum, gastric fluid, nasopharyngeal aspirate, and stool specimens may be used. This is a conditional recommendation with low certainty of evidence for sputum accuracy and very low certainty for other specimen types. 16. In children with signs and symptoms of pulmonary TB in settings with a pretest probability below 5% and an Xpert Ultra negative result on the initial test, repeated testing with Xpert Ultra in sputum or nasopharyngeal aspirate specimens may not be used. This is a conditional recommendation with very low certainty of evidence for test accuracy. 17. In adults in the general population with either signs or symptoms of TB or chest radiograph abnormalities, Xpert MTB/RIF or Xpert Ultra may replace culture as the initial test for pulmonary TB. This is a conditional recommendation with low certainty of evidence for Xpert MTB/RIF accuracy and moderate certainty for Xpert Ultra accuracy. 18. In adults in the general population with a positive TB symptom screen or chest radiograph abnormalities, one Xpert Ultra test may be used rather than two Xpert Ultra tests as the initial test for pulmonary TB. This is a conditional recommendation with very low certainty of evidence for test accuracy.
